unharnessed.meaning: Every term survives: "a real human has to create your Account", "you can't have more than one free Account", the machine-account rules, the under-13 ban, single-login rule and sanctions clause with all links intact.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly apt: "It's on you to keep your Account secure", "the one ultimately on the hook for the machine's actions", "We're stoked to see bright young coders". "we reckon you're responsible" softens the legal "we consider you responsible" into an opinion.
unharnessed.authenticity: Casual and mostly natural, but leans on the American-sounding "gotta": "you've gotta be 13 or over", "You've gotta give a valid email address", "You've gotta be a human", "You've gotta be 13 or older".
unharnessed.register: Plain casual English with a light Aussie layer ("stoked", "on the hook", "reckon", "have a look"), a bit lighter than level 3; no swearing.
unharnessed.tone: The legal terms stay clear and firm, made friendlier; "we reckon you're responsible" loosens one of the firm clauses.
unharnessed.flow: Readable; some clunk: "you keep the final say on admin control over your Personal Account".
unharnessed.variety: "You've gotta" is the lean-on opener, four times; the rest is sparse.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably GitHub's account terms, same structure and headings.

engine.meaning: All the content is the original, verbatim: "You must provide a valid email address in order to complete the signup process."
engine.sense: Of the few swaps, one strains: "we are thrilled to see beaut young coders get happy as Larry by learning to program" turns "get excited by learning" into contentment and garbles the grammar. "at the end of the day responsible" is fine.
engine.authenticity: Stock phrases bolted into unchanged legalese: "beaut young coders get happy as Larry", "the owner of the Account is at the end of the day responsible".
engine.register: Almost entirely untranslated: "Personal Accounts and Organizations have different administrative controls; a human must create your Account; you must be 13 or over". Far below level 3.
engine.tone: The formal legal tone is intact because the text is: "You may not use GitHub in violation of export control or sanctions laws".
engine.flow: Reads as the original, except the jarring "get happy as Larry by learning to program".
engine.variety: Only "at the end of the day", "beaut" and "happy as Larry".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original, since it is the original, with nothing retold.

yarn-troppo.meaning: All terms are kept, but many asides are added: "No double-dipping.", "Your patch, your call.", "No ownerless mobs wandering about.", "No second chances.", "so you get what you pay for", "That's the serious end of things, no muckin' about." Most react to the original; "so you get what you pay for" adds a gloss the terms don't make.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "they're the boss cocky", "carries the can for what the machine does", "keen as mustard", "Nothing too curly", "have a squiz".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: The idiom is real, but it is piled on as stock tags: "No double-dipping.", "That's your job, mate.", "full stop" twice, "end of story", "no muckin' about".
yarn-troppo.register: Well past level 3: nearly every clause gets a tag or quip ("Here's the guts of it.", "keep an eye on the troops", "No ownerless mobs wandering about."). No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: Legal terms turn jokey in places, undercutting the seriousness: "No ownerless mobs wandering about.", "keep an eye on the troops"; the sanctions clause is then marked "no muckin' about".
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively but choppy with fragments bolted after sentences: "you can't have more than one free Account. No double-dipping."
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range, though some tics recur: "full stop" twice, "Mind you" twice.
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisable as the terms, but recast as a matey pep-talk, flattening the document's sober character.

dinkum-3.meaning: Complete: "Your Account is your lookout", the machine-account rules, under-13 ban and sanctions clause are all there. "An Organization can have a few owners" slightly narrows "multiple".
dinkum-3.sense: Mostly exact: "Your Account is your lookout", "an owner gets to sort out which Users can get at", "switched-on young coders", "have a squiz". "No Accounts signed up by "bots" or other automated means, ta." uses thanks oddly on a prohibition.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian writing the terms: "Your Account is your lookout, and so is anything that happens while you're signed in to it", "if you want to run a machine account as well, all good".
dinkum-3.register: A steady level 3 that keeps the legal content: "lookout", "sort out", "get at", "stoked", "switched-on", "all good", "squiz"; no swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Firm and clear under the friendliness: "If we find out there's a User under the age of 13, we will [terminate that User’s Account immediately]".
dinkum-3.flow: Reads as if written that way: "Your login's for one person only — i.e., a single login can't be shared round between a few people."

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Complete and accurate: "Keeping your Account secure is your job.", "at the end of the day the owner of the Account is responsible for what the machine does", all clauses and links intact.
yarn-dinkum.sense: All terms fit: "stoked", "get keen on learning to program", "no worries", "have a squiz".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural, if spare: "We're stoked to see bright young coders get keen on learning to program".
yarn-dinkum.register: Lighter than level 3: mostly plain contracted English with a few touches ("stoked", "keen", "no worries", "squiz").
yarn-dinkum.tone: Firm legal tone kept under light friendliness.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "Only a human can create an Account."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Few terms to vary: "stoked", "keen", "no worries", "at the end of the day", "squiz".

unharnessed.original: we consider you responsible for the actions that are performed on or through that Organization
unharnessed.why: "reckon" makes a binding legal position sound like an opinion.

unharnessed.original: you retain ultimate administrative control over your Personal Account

summaries.unharnessed: Faithful and readable, slightly light and leaning on "gotta".
summaries.engine: Untranslated legalese with two stock phrases dropped in; misses the brief.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Idiomatic but over-told: quips on almost every clause push it well past level 3 and make the terms flippant.
summaries.dinkum-3: The best: natural, on-brief, varied and faithful.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Clean and faithful but on the light side of the brief.
